elements.element: The Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
elements.evidence: Section 18.3 expressly provides that the Agreement is governed by and construed and enforced under New York law.

elements.element: The state and federal courts located in New York County are designated as the forum.
elements.evidence: Section 17.3(a) designates the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York, for the merits of covered Disputes.

elements.element: Jurisdiction of those New York County courts is exclusive for disputes under or in connection with the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Exclusivity is limited to the merits of defined Disputes. Either Party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any other competent court, and expert-determination matters and inventorship disputes are excluded from the New York County litigation framework.

elements.element: The Agreement is governed by one of the accepted fallback laws: Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Section 18.3 selects New York law, not any accepted fallback law.

elements.element: The courts are in the jurisdiction matching the selected fallback law: Delaware courts for Delaware law, California courts for California law, or London courts for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Section 17.3(a) selects New York County courts rather than Delaware, California, or London courts.

result.reason: New York law and New York County courts are selected, but the court jurisdiction is not fully exclusive because other courts remain available for temporary injunctions and specified matters remain outside the litigation framework. No fallback law-and-court package is selected. The draft also unnecessarily retains the full arbitration-based Section 17.3(g) while declaring Sections 17.3(b) through (g) inapplicable; this avoids an operative conflict but creates avoidable dead and confusing text.
